summary: The node scripts Set-OllamaLoopback.ps1 and Move-OllamaProtected.ps1 wrote the transcript of their elevated run next to themselves; run from a repository checkout it landed untracked in agent/ with computer and user names, configuration paths and remote addresses, one 'git add -A' away from a public commit. Both now start it through one helper, Start-RunTranscript: the agent's default log folder (logs next to the configuration named on the SkirnirAgent service command line, which the agent restricts to SYSTEM, Administrators and its service account in applyRules), else the TEMP folder of the elevated account; a 'Log:' line before STATE names the file. The folder is derived only from the service configuration (administrators only) and checked with Directory.Exists (no exception as control flow); Start-Transcript keeps its marked boundary catch. The file name uses [Environment]::MachineName instead of the caller-settable %COMPUTERNAME%. .gitignore ignores leftovers of both scripts. Traced: elevation re-launch and caller message, Finish (Log line before STATE, transcript stopped before exit), the shared helper under dot-sourcing in Move-OllamaProtected, the agent's log-folder default (config.go applyDefaults), the config-folder ACL (install_windows.go applyRules), the LOCAL SERVICE grant logic for first-level folders under the data folder (childidentity_windows.go classifyAccess) and the agent's lumberjack rotation (deletes only its own backups). No router, agent binary, configuration schema, authentication or network path changes.

findings.evidence: Set-OllamaLoopback.ps1:245 and Move-OllamaProtected.ps1:188 on origin/main build the transcript path from $PSScriptRoot; a repository review on 2026-11-12 found such a transcript untracked in a checkout's agent/ folder. .gitignore had no rule for it.
findings.resolution: Transcript moved to the agent's log folder (administrators only) or the elevated account's TEMP folder through Start-RunTranscript; .gitignore ignores /agent/Set-OllamaLoopback-*.log and /agent/Move-OllamaProtected-*.log; both self-tests fail on the old scripts and pass on the new ones, and on Windows a real transcript is written outside the checkout (ADR-0089).

findings.evidence: With install.account set (NT SERVICE\SkirnirAgent), the service account has modify on the configuration folder and could replace logs with a junction, so the elevated script would create its .log transcript elsewhere. In the TEMP fallback with UAC admin-approval mode the unelevated half of the same administrator owns TEMP. A child naming a path inside logs in env/args gets modify on logs through ADR-0088's grants (operator configuration).
findings.resolution: Not introduced by this change: before it, the elevated run wrote into the script folder, which in a checkout is writable by the non-elevated user. The primitive is creating a new, timestamped .log file with non-attacker content; the service account already writes the agent's own logs there, and UAC split tokens of one administrator are not a security boundary. Over-the-shoulder elevation uses the administrator account's own TEMP.

selftest_ollama_protected: all passed in both shells

tests.command: Set-OllamaLoopback.cmd / Move-OllamaProtected.cmd elevated on a node
tests.evidence: Needs an interactive UAC prompt and changes the node; the elevated branch (agent log folder chosen, Log: line in the elevated window) was not exercised. Get-AgentLogFolder was checked against the real SkirnirAgent service command line of a development machine (C:\ProgramData\skirnir-agent\logs), and the non-elevated fallback to TEMP there.
No router code changed; the end-to-end suite does not exercise the node scripts.

limitations: The elevated run was not executed (UAC); the agent-log-folder branch is covered by the pure derivation test and the Directory.Exists check, not by a real elevated transcript.
Transcripts written by earlier versions stay in agent/ of existing checkouts until the operator deletes them; the new .gitignore rules keep them out of commits.
Linux pwsh in CI covers only the pure parts; the host-side transcript check runs in the Windows PowerShell 5.1 CI job.
